projects.description: N-Body Electromagnetic Coupling — SU(2)/SU(3) gauge theory with topological fixed-point projection.
projects.purpose: hamliton: N-Body Electromagnetic Coupling — SU(2)/SU(3) gauge theory with topological fixed-point projection. (Physics / Electromagnetics).
readmeHeadings: # Hamilton Tensor: N-Body Electromagnetic Coupling via Topological Fixed-Point Projection
readmeLead: # Hamilton Tensor: N-Body Electromagnetic Coupling via Topological Fixed-Point Projection

We present the **Hamilton Tensor**, a framework for predicting electromagnetic (EM) coupling in N-body cavity systems without numerically solving Maxwell's equations. Given the E/H field fingerprints of N coupled EM cavities, the Hamilton Tensor learns a unified coupling operator H such that all N body signatures converge to a shared Banach fixed point under repeated application of H. The tensor operates in a Hilbert space spanned by topological fingerprints (persistent homology barcodes) of each body's field distribution, enabling O(N) subspace iteration that bypasses the exponential complexity (d^N) of naive N-body simulation. We validate the framework on synthetic waveguide arrays, cavity QED systems, plasmonic nanoclusters, and circuit QED architectures. The approach achieves a mean Hamilton score of 0.87 on held-out test configurations and converges to machine epsilon (1.8 × 10⁻¹⁶) within 500 iterations. **Keywords:** N-body electromagnetic coupling, Banach fixed-point theorem, topological fingerprinting, persistent homology, tensor product Hilbert space, cavity QED, plasmonic nanoclusters

readmeHeadings: # TopoBridge-Q: Homologically Protected Information Transfer on Quantum Hardware
readmeLead: # TopoBridge-Q: Homologically Protected Information Transfer on Quantum Hardware
**Status:** Experimentally verified on IBM Quantum (ibm_marrakesh, ibm_fez)

TopoBridge-Q implements a quantum protocol for transferring information through a topological bridge Hamiltonian, where the message is encoded as a homology cycle of a simplicial complex. The protocol demonstrates that cycle-encoded information recovers on the opposite register with higher fidelity when the bridge coupling is active than when it is turned off. This effect was measured on two independent IBM quantum processors with classically verified certificates (boundary residual = 0, homology witness = 1).
This is not a physical wormhole. It is a quantum information protocol where topology provides the algebraic structure for encoding, transfer, and verification.

projects.purpose: aether-wave: > **"A high-performance, GPU-accelerated audio engine designed to end the era of 'AI slop' and CPU-bound lag. It is a real-time physics simulation that happens to produce sound. readmeLead: > **"A high-performance, GPU-accelerated audio engine designed to end the era of 'AI slop' and CPU-bound lag. It is a real-time physics simulation that happens to produce sound. By moving the entire DSP pipeline to the GPU and using direct-to-NIC hardware paths, AETHER-WAVE achieves a level of 'sovereignty' over the audio signal that standard DAW architectures simply cannot touch."**

AETHER-WAVE (Architect 2.0) is not a synthesizer in the traditional sense; it is a **Physical Computing Environment** for the modern musician. While standard digital plugins rely on static lookup tables and simplified DSP coefficients, AETHER-WAVE leverages the raw power of your GPU to model the **Acoustic Reality** of the sound itself.

*   **Infinite Harmonic Complexity**: Standard oscillators produce "perfect" waves that often feel sterile. AETHER-WAVE uses **3D FDTD (Finite-Difference Time-Domain)** methods to simulate the physical vibration of molecules. This produces a natural, organic **Harmonic Series** that shifts and evolves as you interact with the wave.

*   **Modal Density & Spectral Depth**: Our reverb and spatial kernels don't just "delay" sound. They simulate **Modal Resonances** of complex geometries. By shifting the "mass" and "tension" of the virtual space, you can move from the crystalline transparency of a glass chamber to the thick, viscous drench of a liquid environment.

readmeLead: **A Toolkit for Persistent Homology Computation and 3D Visualization**

readmeLead: **Context window optimization via stochastic resonance — adaptive noise injection for LLM training.**

Stochastic resonance (SR) is a phenomenon in which the performance of a nonlinear system improves when a moderate level of noise is added to a sub-threshold signal. Originally observed in paleoclimate dynamics (Benzi et al., 1981) and subsequently documented across neural systems, SR has found application in computational optimization where noise can help escaping shallow local minima.

This CLI implements **adaptive stochastic resonance injection** for training signal paths. The core observation is that during LLM training, certain context windows enter saturated states where gradient information becomes sub-threshold. Injecting calibrated noise into these signal paths can temporarily amplify weak signals, improving propagation through saturated layers and accelerating convergence.

readmeHeadings: # VEC-SIMD: Hand-Written SIMD Math Library in Pure x86_64 Assembly
readmeLead: # VEC-SIMD: Hand-Written SIMD Math Library in Pure x86_64 Assembly
**AVX-512 vector math — Mandelbrot, matrix multiply, dot product, FFT — hand-optimized assembly with zero dependencies.**

We present `VEC-SIMD`, a pure x86_64 assembly vector math library written for AVX-512 (Skylake and later). The library implements fundamental linear algebra primitives — dot product, matrix multiplication, Fourier transform — entirely in hand-written SIMD assembly with explicit control over register allocation, instruction scheduling, and memory layout. We demonstrate that hand-optimized SIMD consistently outperforms compiler auto-vectorization by 20–40% on these workloads, and that the gap widens to 2–3× on memory-bandwidth-bound operations like FFT and dot product with large strides. The library has zero C dependencies and is callable from Rust via LLVM's inline ASM syntax or from C via a minimal FFI header.

readmeHeadings: # PGTABLE-ASM: x86_64 Page Table Manipulation in Pure Assembly
readmeLead: # PGTABLE-ASM: x86_64 Page Table Manipulation in Pure Assembly
**Hand-written x86_64 long mode page tables — recursive mapping, huge pages, KPTI, and PCID — all in NASM assembly.**

We present `PGTABLE-ASM`, a pure x86_64 assembly implementation of the full x86_64 long-mode paging subsystem: 4-level page table setup, recursive page table mapping, huge page support (1 GiB and 2 MiB pages), Kernel Page Table Isolation (KPTI), Process Context Identifiers (PCID), and a self-mapping design that allows the kernel to read its own page tables without entering the mapping. The implementation is 1,247 lines of NASM assembly with zero C dependencies — every page table entry is hand-computed, every TLB invalidation is explicit. The project serves as both a reference implementation of x86_64 paging architecture and a building block for kernels that need fine-grained control over memory isolation.

readmeHeadings: # Hollow-ASM: Bare-Metal Kernel for Topological Operating Systems Research
readmeLead: # Hollow-ASM: Bare-Metal Kernel for Topological Operating Systems Research
**A #![no_std] Rust microkernel with x86_64 assembly runtime, persistent homology scheduling, and sub-nanosecond I/O — built for research into topology-grounded operating system design.**

We present `Hollow-ASM`, a bare-metal microkernel written in Rust with hand-written x86_64 assembly runtime components. The kernel explores a foundational question in operating system design: can the scheduler, memory allocator, and I/O subsystem be grounded in topological invariants rather than classical queue-theoretic abstractions? We implement a prototype where scheduling priority is determined by a **persistence landscape distance** between a task's recent memory-access topology and the system-wide topological state, replacing the traditional runqueue. The I/O subsystem achieves sub-nanosecond decision latency via a **SIMD-parallelized telemetry extraction loop** in pure assembly, bypassing the kernel's own scheduling on the fast path. The result is a microkernel capable of < 3ns end-to-end I/O decision cycles on commodity x86_64 hardware, demonstrating that topological scheduling is not merely theoretically interesting but practically competitive with classical designs.

readmeHeadings: # Topo-ASM: Topological Manifolds in x86_64 SIMD Assembly
readmeLead: # Topo-ASM: Topological Manifolds in x86_64 SIMD Assembly
**SIMD-parallelized persistent homology on Vietoris–Rips filtrations — in pure x86_64 assembly.**

We present `topo-asm`, a library for computing persistent homology of Vietoris–Rips filtrations entirely in x86_64 AVX-512 assembly — no Python, no C, no managed runtime. The core insight is that the bottleneck in persistent homology computation is pairwise distance comparison across N(N−1)/2 point pairs, and this is embarrassingly parallel: AVX-512 processes 16 float64 values per cycle. We implement the full filtration pipeline — distance matrix construction, pairwise-clearing simplex enumeration, boundary matrix reduction — in hand-written, cache-aligned SIMD assembly targeting the Haswell/Tremport microarchitectures. The result is a 12× speedup over the state-of-the-art Python implementation (ripser) and a 3× speedup over the C++ baseline, at identical numerical output. The library is callable from Python via a minimal ctypes wrapper, and from Rust via a no_std FFI interface.

readmeLead: **Geometric State Transfer via Topological Surgery on Hollow Manifolds**

The dominant bottleneck in large language model inference is not arithmetic — it is sequential context loading. For a sequence of N tokens, the KV-cache attention mechanism requires O(N²) operations. This work addresses that bottleneck at the geometric level rather than the algorithmic one.

We present Epsilon, a framework for **O(P) geometric state transfer between autonomous agents**, where P is a constant bounded by the payload point budget (P ≤ 64). The approach rests on three independently established results: the Johnson-Lindenstrauss dimensionality reduction lemma, the homology of the 2-sphere, and Chebyshev's inequality applied to memory liveness estimation.

readmeHeadings: ### Training Your First Model (Mac with Apple Silicon)
### Scaling Up to a Remote Machine
readmeLead: **OpenAI Model Craft Challenge: Parameter Golf** is a challenge to train the best language model that fits in a 16MB artifact and trains in under 10 minutes on 8xH100s, evaluated by compression on the FineWeb validation set (tokenizer-agnostic, bits per byte).

This challenge is heavily inspired by the [NanoGPT Speedrunning](https://github.com/KellerJordan/modded-nanogpt) challenge, where participants compete to train a model that reaches 3.28 FineWeb validation loss as quickly as possible. We're excited to see how optimizing for a parameter-constrained setting pushes people toward unique architectures (test-time compute, aggressive parameter tying, depth recurrence, low-rank training, ...), compression schemes (low precision, QAT, bitnets, novel tokenizers, ...), and other creative submissions (test-time training, long context, megakernels ...).

If you're familiar with [neural scaling laws](https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.08361), you can consider this challenge a form of L(N) optimization, where the objective is to optimize the lowest loss given a fixed number of parameters (N) unconstrained by data, compute, steps, or architecture. Challenges like the [NanoGPT Speedrun](https://github.com/KellerJordan/modded-nanogpt), which optimizes for a form of L(T) (~lowest time given constrained loss) or the [NanoGPT Slowrun](https://github.com/qlabs-eng/slowrun), which optimizes for L(D) (lowest loss given constrained dataset size), can be thought of as equivalent challenges in this family.

Ideally, we'd allow for submissions to use arbitrary computational resources. But in order to make the challenge not inaccessibly expensive, we're limiting *leaderboard submissions* to 10 minutes on 8xH100s. However, we'd still love to see submissions that don't meet the compute limitation requirements in our 'Non-record Submissions' section: We're excited to see people push the infinite frontier of parameter limited performance as well.

We also know compute is expensive, so **OpenAI is sponsoring $1,000,000 in compute credits** to help people get started training their models. To request a compute grant, use this form: [Request a Compute Grant](https://openai.com/index/parameter-golf/#credit-form).
When requesting compute, please make sure you choose the appropriate level, write sufficient justification, and **submit with an email tied to a OpenAI / ChatGPT account**.

I built this because I am always hardware-constrained, and I wanted to help my friends out who also run on absolute peasant hardware (16GB RAM + 8GB VRAM). projects.name: DirectStorage
projects.description: DirectStorage for Windows is an API that allows game developers to unlock the full potential of high speed NVMe drives for loading game assets.
projects.purpose: DirectStorage: DirectStorage for Windows is an API that allows game developers to unlock the full potential of high speed NVMe drives for loading game assets. (Compiler / Programming Language).
readmeLead: DirectStorage is a feature intended to allow games to make full use of high-speed storage (such as NVMe SSDs) that can can deliver multiple gigabytes a second of small (eg 64kb) data reads with minimal CPU overhead.  Although it is possible to saturate a drive using traditional ReadFile-based IO the CPU overhead increases non-linearly as the size of individual reads decreases.  Additionally, most games choose to store their assets compressed on disk in order to reduce the install footprint, with these assets being decompressed on the fly as load time.  The CPU overhead of this becomes increasingly expensive as bandwidth increases.

Video game consoles such as the XBox Series X|S address these issues by offloading aspects of this to hardware - making use of the NVMe hardware queue to manage IO and hardware accelerated decompression.  As we expect to see more titles designed to take advantage of the possibilities offered by this architecture it becomes important that Windows has similar capabilities.
The DirectStorage API already exists on Xbox and in order to ease porting of titles between Xbox and Windows, the two APIs are as similar as possible.
You can find some good starting information in [Developer Guidance](Docs/DeveloperGuidance.md)
We invite you to join us at our [discord server](http://discord.gg/directx). See the [related links](##-Related-links) section for our full list of Direct3D 12 and DirectStorage-related links.
